name: F01 buildCellVdoc: the first body line is not floored (the pre-cure bound)
why: a start of 0.5 makes the loop start on 1.5 and `lines[1.5].trim()` throws; -5e-324 + 1 rounds to 1, so line 0 is dropped

name: F02 buildCellVdoc: the first body line is the CEIL of the start
why: a start of 0.5 begins the body on line 2, where the rule `i > 0.5` begins it on line 1

name: F03 buildCellVdoc: the first body line is the floor of start + 1
why: the sum rounds first: -5e-324 + 1 is 1, so a start of -5e-324 drops line 0 that `i > -5e-324` keeps

name: F04 buildCellVdoc: the first body line is the TRUNC of the start
why: trunc(-0.5) is -0, so a start of -0.5 begins the body on line 1, where `i > -0.5` begins it on line 0

name: F05 buildCellVdoc: the last body line is the CEIL of the sum
why: a start of 0.5 over two lines ends the body on line 3, where `i <= 2.5` ends it on line 2

name: F06 buildCellVdoc: the last body line is the floor of the start plus the count
why: the floor of the start before the sum: 1.9999999999999998 + 2 rounds to 4 (a tie, to even), floor(1.9999999999999998) + 2 is 3

name: F07 buildCellVdoc: the last body line is floored (a respelling)
why: EQUIVALENT: the loop compares it only with a whole `i`, and `i <= last` is `i <= floor(last)` for a whole `i` (NaN fails both); the cure at 2c85c77 had this floor and 5f6c7fc dropped it

name: R35 createCellVdocBuilder: the text is read when the builder is made
why: the text is read when the builder is made: the provider makes a builder on every `provideDocumentSymbols` call and most documents hold no cell; 223 to 344 ms per construction on a 130,000-line, 4.29 MB prose document (the review's measurement). Killed by the laziness rows: a text whose `split` throws is not read at construction, a Proxy text records no read, three builders over 130,000 lines of prose cost under 50 ms

name: R38 createCellVdocBuilder: build caches by the cell object

why: build cached by the cell object: the old function read the cell's fields on every call, so a Cell whose code, engine or start line changes between two builds is built from its current fields; the model's cells are never mutated by the project, but the docstring says `byte for byte` for every Cell. Killed by the row that changes one Cell three times (it was argued equivalent in the review round)

name: R16 buildCellVdoc: whitespace is a hand-written class (space, tab, CR, NBSP, U+2028)
why: a hand-written class of five characters: a body line of only U+3000, U+FEFF, U+2029, a vertical tab, a form feed or U+2003 is whitespace to `trim` and content to the class, so the python mute differs. Killed by the whitespace rows, one per character `trim` strips that can stand alone in a body line (23, from a run over U+0000 to U+FFFF: 25 stripped, less the line feed and the carriage return); it survived every row of 89d38e3, which held five of them

name: R27 buildCellVdoc: the engine is read case-insensitively
why: a `{Python}`, `{PYTHON}` or `{pYthon}` cell is muted: the language map is case-sensitive (`cellLanguageId('Python')` is null), so such a cell gets no mute and keeps its body. Not reachable by a user (the Outline never builds a cell whose engine does not map); killed by the engine-case row, which states the three vdocs
